TODAY'S METHOD MAP

五类题共用一条主线：先看结构，再用证据作答

七选五看句子放在哪；完形看哪个词让上下文顺起来；D篇看原文证据；语法填空先判断空格在句子里缺什么。不要先逐词翻译全文。

判断题型任务→找空前后或原文证据→代回检查

七选五：一句话必须接通两边

先看位置段首常总领，段尾常总结或过渡，段中必须同时承上启下。
再看人话线索this / they 指谁？重复词谈的是不是同一件事？however / therefore 的方向对不对？
最后放回只能接通一边的选项，即使有相同单词也要删。

完形：先让故事说得通

先跳过选项通读，抓人物、事件和态度变化。第二遍用三层证据：上下文词义、前后逻辑、固定搭配。四个词都认识时，选最符合整段发展的一项。

  • 语义是否贴合场景
  • 褒贬方向是否一致
  • 主谓宾搭配是否自然
  • 是否照应后文复现

D篇：答案必须能指回原文

每段先用一句话说功能：提出问题、描述实验、呈现结果、限制结论、解释概念、提出建议。细节题找同义改写；推断题只走原文允许的一小步；标题要同时覆盖研究和结论。

语法填空：有提示词看变化，无提示词看结构

有提示词

动词：谓语时态语态 / 非谓语；名词：单复数；形容词：副词或比较级；词根：词性转换。

无提示词

缺主干连接：从句引导词；缺限定：冠词、代词；缺关系：介词、并列连词。

三遍复查

第一遍看句子成分，第二遍看时间和逻辑，第三遍检查拼写、单复数和大小写。

七选五 1

What a Repair Café Really Repairs

维修咖啡馆真正修复的是什么｜主题：社区互助与技能传递

5空｜建议 8—10 分钟｜无小标题｜段中、段尾、段首与承上启下混合
词汇范围：688＋U1—U7
先看空位，再读空前空后；点击任意英文词可开词卡。

People often imagine repair as a private service: a broken object is handed to an expert and later returned in working condition. A repair café follows a different model. Local volunteers bring basic tools, while visitors arrive with lamps, chairs, radios or clothes that need attention.

Visitors do not simply leave an object at the door. _____36_____ That difference turns a quick repair into an exchange of knowledge.

The volunteer usually begins by asking what happened before the object stopped working. Was there a strange sound? Did the lamp flash? Had the chair become less stable over time? These questions help locate the cause before anyone reaches for a tool. _____37_____

_____38_____

A useful repair begins with the owner’s account. A scratch may show that a device was dropped, while a bitter smell may point to an electrical problem. The story does not replace inspection, but it gives the repairer a practical starting point and prevents unnecessary work.

Many cafés also keep a simple record of each case: the symptom, the cause, the action taken and the final result. _____39_____ Future volunteers can search the record when they meet a similar obstacle.

_____40_____ When people watch a repair closely, they learn that failure is often understandable rather than mysterious. They may not become experts in one afternoon, but they leave more willing to examine, maintain and reuse what they own. In this way, the café repairs confidence as well as objects.

选项

每个选项最多使用一次；解密后可查看中文。

A
The question slows the process, but it also makes the hidden reasoning visible.
译这个问题会让过程慢下来，但也会让隐藏的推理变得清楚可见。
B
This record becomes useful long after the object is working again.
译即使物品已经恢复工作，这份记录在很久以后仍然有用。
C
Most electrical devices should therefore be replaced at once.
译因此，大多数电器都应该立刻更换。
D
Instead, they sit beside volunteers and watch each decision.
译相反，他们坐在志愿者旁边，观察每一个判断。
E
Some visitors mainly come because the coffee is inexpensive.
译一些来访者主要是因为咖啡便宜才来。
F
Begin with the story of the object.
译先从物品的故事开始。
G
The final lesson concerns the value of shared skill.
译最后一课关系到共享技能的价值。

本篇全文翻译与整篇复盘

全文逐段翻译（已填正确答案）

01

人们常把维修想象成一种私人服务：把坏掉的物品交给专家，之后再取回恢复正常的物品。维修咖啡馆采用的是另一种模式。当地志愿者带来基本工具，来访者则带着需要处理的台灯、椅子、收音机或衣物。

02

来访者并不是把物品放在门口就离开。相反，他们坐在志愿者旁边，观察每一个判断。这种差别把一次快速维修变成了知识交流。

03

志愿者通常先询问物品停止工作前发生了什么：有没有奇怪的声音？台灯是否闪烁过？椅子是否逐渐变得不稳？这些问题帮助人们在拿起工具之前先确定原因。

04

这个问题会让过程慢下来，但也会让隐藏的推理变得清楚可见。

05

先从物品的故事开始。

06

有效的维修要从物主的讲述开始。一道划痕可能说明设备摔过，而刺鼻的气味可能指向电路问题。讲述不能代替检查，但它能给维修者一个实际的起点，并避免不必要的工作。

07

许多维修咖啡馆还会为每个案例保留简单记录：故障表现、原因、采取的行动和最终结果。即使物品已经恢复工作，这份记录在很久以后仍然有用。以后志愿者遇到相似障碍时，就能查询这份记录。

08

最后一课关系到共享技能的价值。

09

当人们近距离观察维修过程时，会发现故障往往可以理解，并不神秘。他们不可能一个下午就成为专家，却会更愿意检查、维护和重复使用自己的物品。这样一来，维修咖啡馆修复的不只是物品，还有人的信心。

七个选项完整翻译

  1. AThe question slows the process, but it also makes the hidden reasoning visible.

    这个问题会让过程慢下来，但也会让隐藏的推理变得清楚可见。

  2. BThis record becomes useful long after the object is working again.

    即使物品已经恢复工作，这份记录在很久以后仍然有用。

  3. CMost electrical devices should therefore be replaced at once.

    因此，大多数电器都应该立刻更换。

  4. DInstead, they sit beside volunteers and watch each decision.

    相反，他们坐在志愿者旁边，观察每一个判断。

  5. ESome visitors mainly come because the coffee is inexpensive.

    一些来访者主要是因为咖啡便宜才来。

  6. FBegin with the story of the object.

    先从物品的故事开始。

  7. GThe final lesson concerns the value of shared skill.

    最后一课关系到共享技能的价值。

七选五 2

A Tiny Garden Can Be a City Laboratory

小花园也能成为城市实验室｜主题：城市生态与观察方法

5空｜建议 8—10 分钟｜无小标题｜段首、段中、段尾与跨段衔接混合
词汇范围：688＋U1—U7
先看空位，再读空前空后；点击任意英文词可开词卡。

_____36_____ A narrow strip beside a car park may contain compacted soil, bits of plastic and very little water. Yet it also receives sunlight, dust, seeds and insects. Because so many forces interact there, the site can reveal how city nature survives under pressure.

The first task is not to plant anything. Students map the area and record its present condition. _____37_____ They also note where rain gathers and where the ground dries first.

Only after this survey do they choose plants. A species that looks beautiful in a photograph may fail if it requires deep, rich soil. Local grasses and small flowering plants are often more stable because they already suit the climate and provide food for nearby insects. _____38_____

For several weeks, students measure change rather than simply admiring growth. They count new leaves, compare soil moisture and photograph the same square from the same angle. A dead plant is not removed from the record. It is evidence that the original strategy needs adjustment.

This habit changes the meaning of success. _____39_____ A useful garden is one that helps students explain why one condition supports life while another becomes an obstacle.

The finished space may be small, but the method can be applied on a larger scale. Students learn to observe before acting, test one change at a time and interpret results without hiding failure. _____40_____

选项

每个选项最多使用一次；解密后可查看中文。

A
The goal is no longer to keep every plant alive at any cost.
译目标不再是不惜代价让每一株植物都活下来。
B
They mark light, shade, litter and existing forms of life on a simple plan.
译他们在简单的平面图上标出光照、阴影、垃圾和现存生命。
C
Even an unattractive piece of ground can support a careful experiment.
译即使一块不美观的土地，也能支持一次严谨的实验。
D
The next phase is to watch how the chosen plants respond.
译下一阶段是观察所选植物如何作出反应。
E
In other words, the garden trains judgement before it improves the landscape.
译换句话说，这座花园在改善景观之前，先训练了判断力。
F
As a result, all local insects will immediately return to the area.
译因此，所有本地昆虫都会立刻回到这个区域。
G
Some students prefer to paint the surrounding walls bright green.
译一些学生更喜欢把周围墙壁刷成鲜绿色。

本篇全文翻译与整篇复盘

全文逐段翻译（已填正确答案）

01

即使一块不美观的土地，也能支持一次严谨的实验。

02

停车场旁一条狭窄的地带可能有被压实的土壤、塑料碎片和极少的水。然而，它也会接收阳光、灰尘、种子和昆虫。由于许多力量在那里相互作用，这个地点能够显示城市自然如何在压力下生存。

03

第一项任务并不是种植任何东西。学生先绘制区域图，并记录它当前的状况。他们在简单的平面图上标出光照、阴影、垃圾和现存生命。他们还要记下雨水聚集在哪里，以及地面哪里最先变干。

04

只有完成调查后，他们才选择植物。照片上看起来很漂亮的品种，如果需要深厚肥沃的土壤，可能会失败。本地草种和小型开花植物通常更稳定，因为它们已经适应当地气候，还能为附近昆虫提供食物。

05

下一阶段是观察所选植物如何作出反应。

06

接下来的几周里，学生测量变化，而不只是欣赏生长。他们统计新叶数量、比较土壤湿度，并从同一角度拍摄同一块方地。枯死的植物不会从记录中删除；它是原先策略需要调整的证据。

07

这种习惯改变了成功的含义。目标不再是不惜代价让每一株植物都活下来。有用的花园，是能够帮助学生解释为什么一种条件支持生命，而另一种条件却会成为障碍的花园。

08

完成后的空间可能很小，但这种方法可以应用到更大的规模。学生学会先观察再行动，一次只测试一种变化，并且不隐藏失败地解释结果。

09

换句话说，这座花园在改善景观之前，先训练了判断力。

七个选项完整翻译

  1. AThe goal is no longer to keep every plant alive at any cost.

    目标不再是不惜代价让每一株植物都活下来。

  2. BThey mark light, shade, litter and existing forms of life on a simple plan.

    他们在简单的平面图上标出光照、阴影、垃圾和现存生命。

  3. CEven an unattractive piece of ground can support a careful experiment.

    即使一块不美观的土地，也能支持一次严谨的实验。

  4. DThe next phase is to watch how the chosen plants respond.

    下一阶段是观察所选植物如何作出反应。

  5. EIn other words, the garden trains judgement before it improves the landscape.

    换句话说，这座花园在改善景观之前，先训练了判断力。

An online claim can travel through a network long before anyone asks whether it is reliable. A confident tone, a dramatic picture or a large number of shares may create the appearance of truth. None of these, however, is evidence by itself.

本篇全文翻译与整篇复盘

全文逐段翻译（已填正确答案）

01

一个网络说法可能在任何人询问它是否可靠之前，就已经通过网络传播开来。自信的语气、戏剧性的图片或大量转发，可能制造真实的外表。然而，这些本身都不是证据。

02

明确它究竟提出了什么说法。

03

先写出需要核查的准确句子。“这种产品很危险”过于笼统。它对谁危险？在什么条件下？达到多少量时危险？准确的说法才能让证据支持或质疑它。

04

接下来，要找到最早能获得的来源，而不是最热门的转发。这一步常常会把你从一条短帖带到完整报告或原始视频。核查信息由谁制作、何时发布，以及原始材料是否完整。

05

比较证据，而不是比较重复出现的标题。

06

一份报告很少能解决复杂问题。要寻找使用不同方法或数据的独立来源。当来源并非彼此抄录时，它们之间的一致才更有力量。

07

意见不一致并不自动意味着某一方不诚实。这种差异可能来自规模、时间或方法。规模更大的研究可能包含不同人群，后来的报告也可能采用更准确的测量方法。

08

最后，要决定你的结论应该有多确定。证据可能足以支持“很可能”，却不足以支持“永远如此”。公正的判断应当在更好信息出现时保持可修正性。

09

负责任的读者会把信心和绝对确定区分开。

完形全文翻译
妮娜在帮助当地公共图书馆整理捐赠图书时，一张褪色的明信片从两页之间露了出来。明信片上是一条狭窄的街道，只写着一句话：“在车站大钟下面见我。”妮娜没有把它扔掉，而是对信息背后的人产生了好奇。邮戳告诉了她城镇名称，但网络搜索几乎没有提供有用信息。于是她联系了那座城镇的图书馆。一位图书管理员回复说，老车站三十年前已经被购物中心取代。妮娜差点就此结束调查。然而，她注意到照片中的街道仍然保留着现代地图上一条道路的大致形状。她决定亲自前往。到达地点后，一位年长的店主立刻认出了明信片。年轻时，他经常在大钟下面等待，并亲眼见过几个家庭迎接远行归来的亲人。他无法确定写信人是谁，但他的记忆把这张私人信息变成了社区生活的一小份见证。妮娜制作了一场展览，把明信片、现代地图和店主的讲述放在一起。她没有假装自己已经解开所有谜团，而是清楚标出哪些已经确认、哪些仍不确定、哪些是通过记忆补充的。参观者很快开始添加自己的照片和故事。展览不断扩充，并不是因为妮娜找到了名人，而是因为她让一个普通物件与许多人的生活产生了联系。她的项目给图书馆带来重要启示：地方历史并不总藏在官方记录里。它可能存在于旧包裹、家庭账单，或者曾被人当作书签的明信片里。当细心的人花时间解释这些物件、核查证据并邀请他人参与时，它们就会变得有价值。妮娜的调查没有带来戏剧性的胜利，却创造了更稳定的成果：一份全镇可以继续修正和扩充的共享记录。最初卡片上的一行字，最终变成了一个活的记忆网络；它依靠的是耐心，而不是运气。
阅读理解 D 篇

When Perfect Directions Make Us Notice Less

当完美导航让我们观察得更少｜主题：导航工具与空间学习

4题｜建议 8—10 分钟
词汇范围：688＋U1—U7
先判断段落作用，再回原文找证据；推断题不能越过原文边界。

1Digital navigation is designed to remove uncertainty. It tells us where to turn, how far to travel and when we have arrived. This efficiency is valuable, especially in an unfamiliar city. Yet a tool can solve the immediate problem while quietly reducing another ability: learning the shape of a place.

2To explore this possibility, a campus research team asked new students to follow one of two routes between the library and a science building. One group received step-by-step phone directions. The other received a simple map showing the main paths, several landmarks and the general destination, but no moving arrow. Both groups reached the building in almost the same amount of time.

3The difference appeared later. When asked to draw the route from memory, the map group located more landmarks and produced a more accurate network of paths. Members of the phone group often remembered individual turns but struggled to show how one part of the campus connected with another. The directions had helped them complete a journey without requiring them to build a wider picture.

4This does not prove that digital navigation damages everyone’s sense of direction. The trial was small, and people use navigation tools in different ways. A passenger may study the screen and compare it with the street, while another person may follow each command without looking beyond the next turn. The effect therefore depends partly on how a user interacts with the tool.

5The researchers describe the useful alternative as productive friction. The phrase does not mean making travel needlessly difficult. It means leaving a small, manageable obstacle that encourages attention. A map requires users to judge their position, connect a landmark with a direction and notice when reality differs from expectation. That extra work can generate knowledge that survives after the journey ends.

6Good design, then, may not always remove every decision. A navigation system could show the whole route before giving detailed instructions, ask users to identify a landmark at an important turn, or invite them to predict the next direction. Such features would still provide support while keeping the traveller mentally active. The aim is not to reject assistance, but to ensure that assistance does not replace observation.

显示答案与详细解析收起答案与详细解析
正确答案 B阅读理解

证据与排除

第三段是结果核心：两组用时接近，但地图组能标更多地标并画出更准确的道路网络。B 概括 connected picture；A 与 almost the same amount of time 矛盾。

校园实验的主要发现是什么？

原文紧接着解释 leaving a small, manageable obstacle that encourages attention，C 是同义改写。productive 表明这种阻力能产生学习价值，并非故障或无意义困难。

35. Which is the best title for the text?

译为什么每位旅行者都需要纸质地图
译穿过大学校园的最快路线

显示答案与详细解析收起答案与详细解析
正确答案 C阅读理解

证据与排除

全文不是反对导航，而是讨论如何在接受帮助时保留观察和空间学习，C 覆盖实验、productive friction 与设计建议。A、D 绝对化，B 只抓实验表面。

题干中文

本文最佳标题是什么？

正确项中文

在辅助导航中保持观察力

D 篇全文翻译
01

数字导航的设计目标是消除不确定性。它告诉我们在哪里转弯、要走多远以及何时到达。这种效率很有价值，尤其是在陌生城市。然而，一种工具可能在解决眼前问题的同时，悄悄削弱另一种能力：学习一个地方的整体结构。

02

为了探索这种可能性，一支校园研究团队让新生沿两条路线中的一条，从图书馆走到科学楼。一组收到手机逐步导航，另一组收到一张简单地图，上面有主要道路、几个地标和大致目的地，却没有移动箭头。两组到达建筑物所用时间几乎相同。

03

差异后来才出现。当被要求凭记忆画出路线时，地图组标出了更多地标，也画出了更准确的道路网络。手机组成员往往记得单独的转弯，却难以说明校园的一部分如何与另一部分连接。导航帮助他们完成了路程，却没有要求他们建立更大的整体图景。

04

这并不能证明数字导航会损害每个人的方向感。实验规模较小，而且人们使用导航工具的方式不同。一名乘客可能会研究屏幕并与街道比较，另一人则可能只遵循每条指令，从不看下一个转弯之外的地方。因此，影响在一定程度上取决于用户如何与工具互动。

05

研究人员把有用的替代方式称为“有益阻力”。这个词并不是说要让出行变得毫无必要地困难，而是保留一个小而可控的障碍，促使人们集中注意。地图要求使用者判断位置，把地标与方向联系起来，并注意现实与预期不同时的情况。这些额外工作能够产生在旅程结束后仍然保留的知识。

06

因此，好的设计未必总要消除每一个判断。导航系统可以先展示完整路线，再给出详细指令；可以要求使用者在重要转弯处识别地标；也可以邀请他们预测下一个方向。这些功能仍能提供帮助，同时让旅行者保持思考。目标不是拒绝帮助，而是确保帮助不会取代观察。

语法填空 1

A Library of Things

物品图书馆｜主题：共享物品与社区联系

10空｜高考题型｜建议 8 分钟
词汇范围：688＋U1—U7
有提示词看词形，无提示词看句子结构；先找谓语，再找非谓语和连接词。

A Library of Things, 1 lends tools and household equipment instead of books, 2 (establish) in a neighbourhood mall three years ago. The organisers wanted 3 (reduce) waste and help residents avoid buying items they would use only once or twice. Before an object enters the collection, volunteers examine it 4 (careful) and write simple instructions. Anyone 5 borrows an item can report a problem through the project website. Since its opening, the library 6 (save) hundreds of useful objects from becoming rubbish. More importantly, it has increased social 7 (interact). Members often meet neighbours from whom they can learn a practical skill. By sharing rather than owning everything, the community has created 8 more flexible system. It is also becoming 9 (stable) as more people donate equipment and time. What began as a small experiment now shows how local action can generate value far beyond 10 original purpose.

语法填空解析区

尚未批改
1无提示词规则：非限制性定语从句

逗号后缺少指代先行词 A Library of Things 的主语，且从句 lends... 信息完整。

用 which 引导非限制性定语从句；that 不能用于这种逗号隔开的非限制性从句。

2establish规则：一般过去时的被动语态

9stable规则：比较级

随着更多人加入，系统与此前状态相比更稳定。

为什么这样填

10无提示词规则：形容词性物主代词

语法填空全文翻译
一家“物品图书馆”不借书，而是借出工具和家用设备。它三年前在社区商场中成立。组织者希望减少浪费，并帮助居民避免购买只会使用一两次的物品。物品进入收藏前，志愿者会认真检查并写下简单说明。任何借用物品的人都可以通过项目网站报告问题。开办以来，这家图书馆已经使数百件有用物品免于变成垃圾。更重要的是，它增加了社会互动。成员经常遇到能够教给自己实用技能的邻居。通过共享而不是拥有一切，社区建立了一个更加灵活的系统。随着更多人捐赠设备和时间，这个系统也变得更加稳定。最初的小实验如今说明，地方行动可以产生远远超出原始目的的价值。
语法填空 2

Letters Along the Mountain Road

山路上的信件｜主题：志愿服务与地方联系

10空｜高考题型｜建议 8 分钟

A small post office 1 (build) beside a mountain road once served twelve villages. For many years, the road 2 (use) by postmen on bicycles, even in bitter winter weather. The office later closed 3 most messages had moved online. Last year, local volunteers reopened the room 4 (carry) letters and medicine to elderly residents who still lived far from the town centre. Each volunteer follows a fixed route and records any obstacle 5 may make the next journey unsafe. The group also keeps 6 (it) bicycles in good condition and checks them 7 (regular). Since the project began, volunteers 8 (collect) dozens of stories about the old postal route. These accounts have become 9 valuable local record. They show that a simple service can create a much 10 (strong) connection when people understand the history behind it.

语法填空全文翻译
山路旁曾经建有一间小邮局，为十二个村庄服务。许多年来，即使在寒冷刺骨的冬季天气里，邮递员也骑自行车走这条路。后来，由于大多数信息转到线上，邮局关闭了。去年，当地志愿者重新开放了这间屋子，为仍住在远离镇中心地区的老年居民运送信件和药物。每位志愿者都沿固定路线行进，并记录可能使下次路程不安全的障碍。团队还让自行车保持良好状态，并定期检查。项目开始以来，志愿者已经收集了几十个关于旧邮路的故事。这些讲述已经成为一份珍贵的地方记录。它们表明，当人们理解一项简单服务背后的历史时，这项服务能够建立更加牢固的联系。

第一部分　七选五

阅读下面短文，从短文后的选项中选出可以填入空白处的最佳选项。选项中有两项为多余选项。

1. What a Repair Café Really Repairs

People often imagine repair as a private service: a broken object is handed to an expert and later returned in working condition. A repair café follows a different model. Local volunteers bring basic tools, while visitors arrive with lamps, chairs, radios or clothes that need attention.

Visitors do not simply leave an object at the door. _____36_____ That difference turns a quick repair into an exchange of knowledge.

The volunteer usually begins by asking what happened before the object stopped working. Was there a strange sound? Did the lamp flash? Had the chair become less stable over time? These questions help locate the cause before anyone reaches for a tool. _____37_____

_____38_____

A useful repair begins with the owner’s account. A scratch may show that a device was dropped, while a bitter smell may point to an electrical problem. The story does not replace inspection, but it gives the repairer a practical starting point and prevents unnecessary work.

Many cafés also keep a simple record of each case: the symptom, the cause, the action taken and the final result. _____39_____ Future volunteers can search the record when they meet a similar obstacle.

_____40_____ When people watch a repair closely, they learn that failure is often understandable rather than mysterious. They may not become experts in one afternoon, but they leave more willing to examine, maintain and reuse what they own. In this way, the café repairs confidence as well as objects.

  1. A. The question slows the process, but it also makes the hidden reasoning visible.
  2. B. This record becomes useful long after the object is working again.
  3. C. Most electrical devices should therefore be replaced at once.
  4. D. Instead, they sit beside volunteers and watch each decision.
  5. E. Some visitors mainly come because the coffee is inexpensive.
  6. F. Begin with the story of the object.
  7. G. The final lesson concerns the value of shared skill.

2. A Tiny Garden Can Be a City Laboratory

_____36_____ A narrow strip beside a car park may contain compacted soil, bits of plastic and very little water. Yet it also receives sunlight, dust, seeds and insects. Because so many forces interact there, the site can reveal how city nature survives under pressure.

The first task is not to plant anything. Students map the area and record its present condition. _____37_____ They also note where rain gathers and where the ground dries first.

Only after this survey do they choose plants. A species that looks beautiful in a photograph may fail if it requires deep, rich soil. Local grasses and small flowering plants are often more stable because they already suit the climate and provide food for nearby insects. _____38_____

For several weeks, students measure change rather than simply admiring growth. They count new leaves, compare soil moisture and photograph the same square from the same angle. A dead plant is not removed from the record. It is evidence that the original strategy needs adjustment.

This habit changes the meaning of success. _____39_____ A useful garden is one that helps students explain why one condition supports life while another becomes an obstacle.

The finished space may be small, but the method can be applied on a larger scale. Students learn to observe before acting, test one change at a time and interpret results without hiding failure. _____40_____

  1. A. The goal is no longer to keep every plant alive at any cost.
  2. B. They mark light, shade, litter and existing forms of life on a simple plan.
  3. C. Even an unattractive piece of ground can support a careful experiment.
  4. D. The next phase is to watch how the chosen plants respond.
  5. E. In other words, the garden trains judgement before it improves the landscape.
  6. F. As a result, all local insects will immediately return to the area.
  7. G. Some students prefer to paint the surrounding walls bright green.

3. How to Judge an Online Claim

An online claim can travel through a network long before anyone asks whether it is reliable. A confident tone, a dramatic picture or a large number of shares may create the appearance of truth. None of these, however, is evidence by itself.

_____36_____

Begin by stating the exact sentence that needs checking. “This product is dangerous” is too general. Dangerous to whom, under what condition and in what amount? A precise claim gives you something that evidence can either support or challenge.

Next, locate the earliest available source rather than the most popular repost. _____37_____ Check who produced the information, when it was published and whether the original material is complete.

_____38_____

One report rarely settles a difficult question. Look for independent sources that used different methods or data. Agreement between sources is stronger when they did not merely copy one another.

Disagreement does not automatically mean that one side is dishonest. _____39_____ A larger study may include a different population, or a later report may use a more accurate measure.

Finally, decide how certain your conclusion should be. Evidence may justify “probably” without justifying “always”. A fair judgement can remain open to revision when better information appears. _____40_____

  1. A. Define what is actually being claimed.
  2. B. Compare evidence, not repeated headlines.
  3. C. The difference may come from scale, timing or method.
  4. D. A responsible reader separates confidence from certainty.
  5. E. This step often leads from a short post to a full report or original video.
  6. F. The safest choice is to distrust every statement on the Internet.
  7. G. Pictures are usually more reliable than written explanations.

第二部分　完形填空

阅读下面短文，从每题所给的 A、B、C、D 四个选项中选出可以填入空白处的最佳选项。

The Postcard Behind the Shelf

Nina was helping the local library sort donated books when a faded postcard _____41_____ from between two pages. It showed a narrow street and carried only one sentence: “Meet me beneath the station clock.” Instead of throwing it away, Nina became _____42_____ about the people behind the message. The postage mark gave her the name of a town, but an Internet search produced almost no useful _____43_____. She then contacted the town library. A librarian replied that the old station had been _____44_____ by a shopping mall thirty years earlier. Nina nearly ended her search there. However, she noticed that the street in the picture still _____45_____ the general shape of a road on the modern map. She decided to visit. At the location, an elderly shop owner _____46_____ the postcard at once. As a teenager, he had often waited under that clock and had _____47_____ several families meeting relatives returning from distant journeys. He could not identify the writer, but his memory changed the postcard from a private message into a small _____48_____ of community life. Nina created a display that placed the postcard beside the modern map and the shop owner’s account. She did not _____49_____ to have solved every mystery. Instead, she clearly marked what was known, what was uncertain and what had been _____50_____ through memory. Visitors soon began adding their own photographs and stories. The display grew, not because Nina had found a famous person, but because she had made an ordinary object _____51_____ to many lives. Her project taught the library an important lesson: local history is not always hidden in official records. It may survive in an old package, a family bill or a postcard that someone once used as a bookmark. 第三部分　阅读理解（D篇）

阅读下面短文，从每题所给的 A、B、C、D 四个选项中选出最佳选项。

When Perfect Directions Make Us Notice Less

Digital navigation is designed to remove uncertainty. It tells us where to turn, how far to travel and when we have arrived. This efficiency is valuable, especially in an unfamiliar city. Yet a tool can solve the immediate problem while quietly reducing another ability: learning the shape of a place.

To explore this possibility, a campus research team asked new students to follow one of two routes between the library and a science building. One group received step-by-step phone directions. The other received a simple map showing the main paths, several landmarks and the general destination, but no moving arrow. Both groups reached the building in almost the same amount of time.

The difference appeared later. When asked to draw the route from memory, the map group located more landmarks and produced a more accurate network of paths. Members of the phone group often remembered individual turns but struggled to show how one part of the campus connected with another. The directions had helped them complete a journey without requiring them to build a wider picture.

This does not prove that digital navigation damages everyone’s sense of direction. The trial was small, and people use navigation tools in different ways. A passenger may study the screen and compare it with the street, while another person may follow each command without looking beyond the next turn. The effect therefore depends partly on how a user interacts with the tool.

The researchers describe the useful alternative as productive friction. The phrase does not mean making travel needlessly difficult. It means leaving a small, manageable obstacle that encourages attention. A map requires users to judge their position, connect a landmark with a direction and notice when reality differs from expectation. That extra work can generate knowledge that survives after the journey ends.

Good design, then, may not always remove every decision. A navigation system could show the whole route before giving detailed instructions, ask users to identify a landmark at an important turn, or invite them to predict the next direction. Such features would still provide support while keeping the traveller mentally active. The aim is not to reject assistance, but to ensure that assistance does not replace observation.

  1. 32. What did the campus trial mainly find?

    B. Map users formed a better connected picture of the campus.
    C. New students preferred printed maps to digital tools.
    D. Landmarks made both groups take longer routes.

  2. 33. What does “productive friction” in paragraph 5 refer to?

    B. A difficult route chosen only to test patience.
    C. A small challenge that keeps the user attentive.
    D. A disagreement between a map and a researcher.

  3. 34. What can be inferred about the writer’s view of navigation tools?

    A. They should be removed from university campuses.
    B. Their influence depends partly on how actively people use them.
    C. They are useful only when travellers already know the route.
    D. Their main purpose should be to make every journey slower.
